label: input token in {u,h,q,e,v,n} (copy phase: when next output is a/o/r/c/k/f/j/d)
explanation: Token-selective unit: activity is almost entirely gated by the current input token being one of u, h, q, e, v, n (rate ordered u 41% > h 31% > q 27% > e 21% > v 14% > n 11%; adding digit 2 gives a small extra share). Those six tokens cover about 93% of activation mass. It never fires at t=0 or on the <DEL> step. In the copy phase it fires much more readily, and most strongly, when the token being output at that step is a, o, r, c, k, f, j or d. The top activations (about 0.23) are the first copy step, where the input is u/e/h and the output is a, e.g. u a ... <DEL> [u] -> a. In the original phase, which occurrences of these tokens fire is only weakly explained: the rate rises with position (orig_idx 4-7) and with certain preceding tokens (h, 1, x, u, 2, q), so it depends on context in ways no simple predicate captures. Precision stays low (about 0.35) because most occurrences of the trigger tokens do not cross threshold. It does not fire on other letters or digits, apart from rare low-magnitude cases.
